applicability_domain.declared_from: the swept geometry, not from where the residuals are small
applicability_domain.note: deployed launches reach 12 waves, beyond the 4 measured; those fall back to the largest measured wave count and score -7.7 to -11.0 percent. M > 64 leaves this program on both the swept grid and the deployed surface, so the M bound is a program boundary rather than a sweep limitation.

form.expression: t_us = fill_us(waves, wave_fill) + split_k_reduction_us + rounds_per_cta * round_service_us
form.interpolation: linear in wave_fill inside a measured wave count; a wave count beyond the measured range falls back to the largest measured one
form.round_service_us: ctas * tile_n * tile_k * dtype_bytes / in_round_gb_s, tile_n = 128
form.units: fill and service in microseconds; in_round_gb_s in GB/s of weight read
form.waves: ceil(ctas / 104), where 104 is the C500 AP count

keyed_on_waves_and_wave_fill.note: the form was fixed before this score was computed and scored once; no functional form, threshold or breakpoint was chosen by looking at the residuals

held_out_score_against_deployed_projecti.known_weakness: the tables pool the swept M values, and the three deployed M=64 cells are the worst at -11.9, -13.6 and -18.6 percent. M=64 is the last M inside this program; above it the vendor selects tn_128x128x128_4m1n8k_256t_4stage

isolation_experiment.design: sweep N so that the same wave fill recurs at different wave counts, with the program identity verified at every point; 72 of 80 cells stayed in the program
isolation_experiment.question: is the rate a function of wave fill alone, or does wave count matter separately?
isolation_experiment.reading: the residual wave-count effect vanishes at full fill and grows as fill falls, so the table is keyed on both. The measurement also supplied the missing low-fill three-wave point (1238 GB/s at fill 0.692), which is why the deployed 224-CTA cells stop running fast

physical_reading: A launch of C CTAs occupies ceil(C / 104) waves on the 104 APs and its last wave is only C mod 104 wide; the idle APs in that partial wave are what depress the achieved weight-read rate. The evidence that this is the right axis rather than raw CTA count: at wave fill 1.00 the rate is 1572 GB/s over one wave and 1562 over three, and scoring the deployed 9.6- and 11.4-wave lm_head cells on fill instead of on CTA count moves them from -12.5% to -3%. This is the per-kernel producers-per-unit quantity that gpu_memory_source declares it cannot supply, measured for one compiled program.

provenance.identity_tool: mcTracer, per-point program identity verified for every swept cell
provenance.workspace: vendor default; CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG / MCBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG / MACA_WORKSPACE unset

status: Measured and held-out scored; beats the current Forward across the whole island. Not yet wired -- wiring is implementation plus three-hardware revalidation, not further measurement.
why_not_wired: Nothing further to measure for this island. What remains is implementation: a C500-gated consumer keyed on the launch signature the canonical GEMM launch selection already carries (tile_m, tile_n, tile_k, split_k, reduction), then the full three-hardware revalidation with A800 and 910B bit-identical. The island is 41.3% of predicted decode GEMM time across the nine C500 TP1 dense cells; the rest of the surface stays on the current path until its own programs are measured.

wiring_form.physical_meaning: the fraction of the device's DRAM capacity a launch achieves when its last wave leaves APs idle. It is the per-kernel producers-per-unit / independent-request quantity gpu_memory_source's own docstring declares it cannot supply, measured for one compiled program.
wiring_form.remaining_work: a C500-gated consumer in the GEMM predictor keyed on the launch signature canonical already carries (tile_m 64, tile_n 128, tile_k 256, split_k, fp32_external reduction), a mechanism entry in configs/hardware/metax_c500.yaml binding this reference by SHA the way the fused-MoE operand pipelines are bound, and the three-hardware revalidation with A800 and 910B bit-identical.
wiring_form.second_order_m_dependence: at matched geometry the round grows 0.6 to 9.2 percent from M=8 to M=64, mostly under 5 percent. It is recorded but not modelled; it is why the three deployed M=64 cells are the worst scored.
wiring_form.statement: The repository's C500 DRAM effective_capacity is flat at 1653.1 GB/s in the number of active units, so it already carries the peak but not the occupancy dependence. The measurement is therefore published as a dimensionless in-round efficiency multiplying that existing capacity, rather than as a replacement rate table.
